hindi: धन से हीन मनुष्य हीन नहीं है, वह धनी है, निश्चयपूर्वक; जो विद्यारत्न से हीन है, वह सभी वस्तुओं में हीन है।
english: One devoid of wealth is not devoid, and he is a rich man, of firm certainty; he who is devoid of the jewel of learning, he is devoid in all things.
notes: suniścayaḥ is taken as a bahuvrīhi 'of firm certainty'; an adverbial sense 'certainly' is possible. The ca after hīnaḥ in line a joins nothing visible in the unit; it is rendered 'and' as printed. Line b gives the contrast: the poor man with learning is not devoid, the man without learning is devoid in all things.

hindi: दृष्टि से पवित्र किया हुआ पैर रखना चाहिए, वस्त्र से पवित्र किया हुआ जल पीना चाहिए, शास्त्र से पवित्र किया हुआ वाक्य बोलना चाहिए, मन से पवित्र किए हुए का आचरण करना चाहिए।
english: The foot purified by sight one should place; the water purified by cloth one should drink; the statement purified by treatise one should speak; what is purified by the mind one should do.

text_flags.why: vākya is a neuter a-stem; the object should be vākyam, agreeing with śāstrapūtam (n. acc.). Possible typo (visarga for anusvāra).

notes: The object of samācaret is not stated; 'what is purified by the mind' is the literal reading of manaḥpūtam as its object.

hindi: यदि सुख का अभिलाषी हो, विद्या को त्याग दे; यदि विद्या का अभिलाषी हो, सुख को त्याग दे। सुख के अभिलाषी को विद्या कहाँ से, विद्या के अभिलाषी को सुख कहाँ से?
english: If one is a seeker of happiness, one should give up learning; if one is a seeker of learning, one should give up happiness. For a seeker of happiness, whence learning? For a seeker of learning, whence happiness?
notes: sukhārthinaḥ and vidyārthinaḥ are genitive singular (dative-like sense 'for').

hindi: कवि क्या नहीं देखते? कौए क्या नहीं खाते? मद्य पीने वाले क्या नहीं बकते? स्त्रियाँ क्या नहीं करतीं?
english: What do poets not see? What do crows not eat? What do drinkers of liquor not babble? What do women not do?

hindi: भाग्य रंक को राजा बनाता है और राजा को रंक ही; और धनी को निर्धन ही, निर्धन को धनी।
english: Fate makes a pauper a king, and a king a pauper indeed; and a rich man wealthless indeed, a wealthless man rich.
notes: The subject vidhiḥ stands at the end of the unit and governs karoti in line a; the verb is not repeated in line b. vidhi is rendered 'fate'.

hindi: लोभियों का शत्रु याचक है, मूर्खों का रिपु उपदेश देने वाला है; उपपति वाली स्त्रियों का शत्रु पति है, चोरों का रिपु चन्द्रमा है।
english: For the greedy the petitioner is an enemy; for fools the one who instructs is a foe; for women with a paramour the husband is an enemy; for thieves the moon is a foe.
notes: Genitives are rendered with 'for'. śatru and ripu are both enemy; 'enemy' and 'foe' are used to mark the alternation. jāra-strī is read as a woman who has a paramour (jāra).

hindi: जिनके न विद्या है, न तप, न दान, न ज्ञान, न शील, न गुण, न धर्म, वे इस मर्त्यलोक में पृथ्वी पर भार बने हुए हैं; मनुष्य के रूप में पशु विचरते हैं।
english: Those who have no learning, no austerity, no giving, no knowledge, no good conduct, no virtue, no dharma, they are a burden on the earth in the mortal world; beasts roam in human form.

text_flags.why: śīla is a neuter a-stem and the other items of the list are nominative; śīlāṃ is not a nominative form. Printed likely for śīlam (nom. n. sg.).

notes: Line c ends in bhārabhūtā for bhārabhūtāḥ: visarga lost before the initial m- of the next line. te and mṛgāḥ are in apposition: those people are the beasts. The verb 'are' in line c is supplied (no verb printed).

words.gloss: of those devoid of inner substance

hindi: भीतर के सार से हीन लोगों के लिए उपदेश उत्पन्न नहीं होता; मलय पर्वत के संसर्ग से बाँस चन्दन-सा नहीं बनता।
english: For those devoid of inner substance, instruction does not arise; from contact with Mount Malaya a bamboo does not become like sandal.
notes: upadeśo na jāyate is read literally as 'instruction does not arise' (does not take effect). candanāyate is a denominative 'acts/becomes like sandal'.

hindi: जिसके पास अपनी प्रज्ञा नहीं है, शास्त्र उसका क्या करता है? दोनों आँखों से हीन का दर्पण क्या करेगा?
english: For whom there is no wisdom of his own, what does a treatise do for him? For one devoid of both eyes, what will a mirror do?
notes: svayam is read with prajñā ('own wisdom').

hindi: दुष्ट को सज्जन बनाने का पृथ्वी पर निश्चय ही कोई उपाय नहीं है; सौ बार धोया हुआ गुदा श्रेष्ठ इन्द्रिय नहीं हो सकता।
english: There is indeed no means on earth to make a wicked man a good man; the anus, washed a hundred times, would not become the best organ.

text_flags.why: śata-dhā 'a hundredfold, a hundred times' is the expected adverb; śātadhā with long ā is not an expected form. Possible typo; metre (16 syllables) is the same either way.

notes: apāna is normally masculine; the printed apānaṃ is taken as the nominative subject of bhavet (form read as neuter). apāna is glossed 'anus' (lower orifice) from the sense with indriya; the alternative 'downward breath' does not suit 'washed'.

words.gloss: from hatred of a trusted person

hindi: आप्तजन से द्वेष से मृत्यु हो सकती है, दूसरे से द्वेष से धन का क्षय; राजा से द्वेष से नाश हो सकता है, ब्राह्मणों से द्वेष से कुल का क्षय।
english: From hatred of a trusted person death would arise; from hatred of another, loss of wealth; from hatred of the king destruction would arise; from hatred of brahmins, ruin of the family.
notes: bhavet is printed with the first and third members and understood with the second and fourth. brahma is read as 'brahmin' (brahman); 'Veda' is a possible alternative for brahma. para = 'another' (other person).

words.gloss: frequented by tigers and chief elephants
partaking of leaves, fruit and water
bark garment worn out a hundredfold

hindi: बाघों और गजराजों से सेवित वन श्रेष्ठ है; वृक्षों में निवास, पत्ते, फल और जल का सेवन, तिनकों पर शय्या, सौ बार जीर्ण वल्कल वस्त्र; न कि बन्धुओं के बीच धनहीन जीवन।
english: Better a forest frequented by tigers and chief elephants, a dwelling among trees, partaking of leaves, fruit and water, a bed on grass, a bark garment worn out a hundredfold; not a life devoid of wealth in the midst of kinsmen.
notes: śata-jīrṇa is read as 'worn out a hundredfold'; 'with a hundred worn places' is a possible alternative. vyāghra-gaja-indra is read as a dvandva (tigers and chief elephants) inside the tat-puruṣa with sevita. Items in lines b to c are in apposition to varaṃ vanaṃ; no verb is printed.

hindi: ब्राह्मण वृक्ष है और उसका मूल सन्ध्या है; वेद शाखा है, धर्मकर्म पत्र हैं। इसलिए मूल की यत्न से रक्षा करनी चाहिए; मूल के कट जाने पर न शाखा ही है, न पत्र।
english: The brahmin is the tree and its root is the twilight rite; the Veda is the branch, acts of dharma the leaf. Therefore the root is to be protected with effort; when the root is cut, there is indeed no branch, no leaf.
notes: sandhyā is the twilight rite (sandhyā worship), the only sense the line supports. dharma-karmāṇi is plural with singular patram; read as a collective. A dvandva 'dharma and actions' is a possible alternative.

hindi: माता कमला देवी हैं और पिता देव जनार्दन हैं; बान्धव विष्णु के भक्त हैं और अपना देश तीनों भुवन है।
english: The mother is the goddess Kamalā, and the father is the god Janārdana; kinsmen are devotees of Viṣṇu, and one's own country is the three worlds.
notes: bāndhavā for bāndhavāḥ: visarga lost before the initial v- of viṣṇu. The placement of ca is as printed (after mātā and after viṣṇubhaktāḥ); it is rendered as joining the two halves of each line. The line does not say whose mother, father, kinsmen or country.

hindi: एक वृक्ष पर बैठे हुए अनेक रंगों के पक्षी प्रातःकाल दसों दिशाओं में जाते हैं; वहाँ क्या वेदना?
english: Birds of various colours, perched on one tree, go at dawn in the ten directions; what pain is there?
notes: The first and second tokens of line a lose their final visarga (ekavṛkṣasamārūḍhā, nānāvarṇā) by sandhi before voiced consonants. tatra is rendered 'there' (in that).

words.gram: caus. ppp. ni-√pat, m. nom. sg.

hindi: जिसके पास बुद्धि है, उसके पास बल है; निर्बुद्धि का बल कहाँ से? वन में जब सिंह उन्मत्त था, मच्छर के द्वारा गिरा दिया गया।
english: He who has intellect, his is strength; for one without intellect, whence strength? In the forest, when the lion was maddened, he was felled by a mosquito.
notes: yadā has no printed correlative (no tadā). unmatta is read 'maddened' (intoxicated or frenzied).

words.gloss: for the life of a child
by service of your lotus feet

hindi: यदि विश्वम्भर हरि का गान किया जाता है, मेरे जीवन में क्या चिन्ता? नहीं तो शिशु के जीवन के लिए माता का दूध कैसे बनाया गया? इस प्रकार बार-बार विचार करके, हे यदुपते, हे लक्ष्मीपते, केवल आपके चरणकमलों की सेवा से मेरे द्वारा काल निरन्तर बिताया जा रहा है।
english: What worry is there in my life if Hari, the sustainer of the world, is sung? If not, how was mother's milk created for the life of a child? Having reflected thus again and again, O lord of the Yadus, O lord of Lakṣmī, only by service of your lotus feet is time continually spent by me.
notes: no cet = 'if not'. nirmame has no printed subject (3 sg. pf. mid.; 1 sg. has the same form); it is read 3 sg. with Hari understood and rendered impersonally ('was created'). muhurmuhuḥ is a repetition 'again and again'. viśvambhara has the m-augment: viśvam-bhara. Hari, Yadupati and Lakṣmīpati are names or epithets; the line does not say more.

words.gloss: in the speech of the gods

hindi: देवताओं की वाणी में मैं विशिष्ट बुद्धि वाला हूँ, फिर भी दूसरी भाषा का लोभी हूँ; जैसे अमरों में सुधा के होते हुए स्वर्ग की स्त्रियों के अधर-रस में रुचि होती है।
english: In the speech of the gods I am of distinguished intellect, nevertheless I am greedy for another language; just as, nectar being among the immortals, there is a liking for the lip-liquor of the heavenly women.
notes: Line a ends 'viśiṣṭabuddhi-' and line b begins 'stathāpi': the s is the visarga of buddhiḥ, written at the start of the next line (buddhiḥ + tathāpi). Therefore the first token of line b is read as tathāpi only. gīrvāṇa-vāṇī is read as 'speech of the gods'. adhara-āsava is 'lip-liquor' (āsava, a distilled drink). The copula 'am' in the first half is supplied.

hindi: अन्न की तुलना में आटा दस गुना है, आटे की तुलना में दूध दस गुना है; दूध की तुलना में मांस आठ गुना है, मांस की तुलना में घी दस गुना है।
english: Compared with grain, flour is tenfold; compared with flour, milk is tenfold; compared with milk, meat is eightfold; compared with meat, ghee is tenfold.

text_flags.why: māṃsa is a neuter a-stem; the nominative subject is māṃsam. The printed form with long ā and anusvāra is not a valid nominative. Likely typo.

notes: The text does not say in what respect each item is 'tenfold' or 'eightfold' (guṇa is used as 'fold'); none is supplied.

hindi: शोक से रोग बढ़ते हैं, दूध से शरीर बढ़ता है; घी से वीर्य बढ़ता है, मांस से मांस खूब बढ़ता है।
english: By grief diseases increase; by milk the body grows; by ghee vigour (vīrya) increases; from meat flesh increases greatly.
notes: rogā for rogāḥ: visarga lost before v-. māṃsa is meat in the first place and flesh in the second; the same word is used twice.
